subject: Renewal: BrightAtlas dedicated pool expansion & throughput guarantees
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Katherine O'Neill <k.oneill@brightatlas.com>, Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@brightatlas.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 30 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: BrightAtlas dedicated pool expansion & throughput guarantees

Katherine — good to reconnect. Per our renewal conversation, BrightAtlas is planning to put the next phase of your search + recommendations workload onto a larger model footprint plus a dedicated reranker. That shift increases memory/compute per-request and drives the need for extra reserved capacity.

Key summary: 
- Current committed pool: 12x A100-equivalent GPUs (24/7 reserved)
- Proposed renewal (24-month term): add 8x H100-class GPUs dedicated to the new 40k-context model (primary inference) and 2x H100-class GPUs for the reranker pool.
- Throughput guarantees: baseline committed throughput of 600 tokens/sec aggregate (p95), with a 2x burst buffer for traffic spikes.
- Fallback plan: routing to smaller model variants if capacity is exhausted; we provide automatic graceful degradation.

Attached is a proposal that lays out pricing, the new SOW, and the timeline for migration (we've included a canary rollout plan and rollback steps). High-level asks from BrightAtlas we'd like to confirm:
1) Approve the 24-month renewal term (pricing options inside).
2) Confirm whether BrightAtlas needs a hard p95 latency SLA (we can include with a premium).
3) Confirm a preferred billing cadence (monthly vs. quarterly).

Next steps: if you confirm the term and throughput targets, we will circulate an updated SOW + DocuSign link. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call today if you want to walk through specifics.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Rishi — thanks for the clear summary and the proposal. A couple quick items from our side before we commit: 

- We are aligned on moving to the larger 40k-context model for our user-facing ranking pipeline; the reranker add-on makes sense for edge cases.
- Can you break out the incremental cost just for the reranker pool (we expect heavy use during business hours only)?
- We need a firm p95 latency target for the primary model (we're aiming for <350ms p95 per request at peak). Please flag if that requirement materially changes pricing.
- Regarding billing: procurement prefers quarterly invoicing and Net30.

If you can send a redlined SOW with the reranker-hours optimization (e.g., daytime-only reserved capacity + autoscale for nights/weekends), we should be able to sign quickly. Also add Tom (infra) to any follow-ups about migration windows.

Best,
Katherine O'Neill
Head of ML Platforms
BrightAtlas
k.oneill@brightatlas.com

Subject: Fwd: BrightAtlas dedicated pool expansion — pricing/SLAs follow-up

Vivek/Priyom — forwarding Katherine's note. Short thread: BrightAtlas wants a p95 <350ms target and prefers quarterly Net30 billing. They also want a daytime-only reserved reranker pool to lower costs (heavy use 9am–6pm PT).

Proposed config (quick numbers):
- Primary inference: +8x H100 (dedicated, 24/7) — supports 40k-context model. Committed throughput 600 tok/s (p95 target depends on kernel/mem; estimate: with H100 and our optimized kernel we can hit ~300–400ms p95 for typical payloads at that throughput; need to add margin).
- Reranker: 2x H100 reserved during 09:00–18:00 PT; autoscale to 0.5x baseline using preemptible capacity evenings/weekends. This should save ~35% on reranker costs vs 24/7 reservation.
- Discount structure: 10% on top-line for 24-month commit + additional 5% for committing to quarterly prepayment (they prefer Net30; we can offer billing credits instead).

Questions for engineering: 
1) Can we guarantee p95 <350ms for the primary at 600 tok/s? If not, what's the required GPU count uplift?
2) Are there optimizations (quantization/kv-cache tweaks) we can apply to lower latency without adding more GPUs?

If we can get a definitive latency confirmation, I'll produce an updated SOW and the DocuSign link. Also thinking we offer a one-month onboarding credit for migration costs. Thoughts?

—Rishi

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 30 Aug 2028 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: BrightAtlas dedicated pool expansion — pricing/SLAs follow-up

Short answers from infra/runtime: 
- With our latest kernel selector and memory-layout optimizations, 8x H100 should be sufficient to meet ~350ms p95 for the primary model at 600 tok/s for their typical request size (avg 1,400 tokens per request). That assumes we enable a 2x per-GPU request batching window and keep KV cache warmed for hot prefixes.
- To give headroom we recommend adding a small buffer: either 1 extra H100 (recommended) or enable a 15% burst SLA that uses preemptible capacity if they hit sustained spikes. The preemptible fallback is cheaper but not SLA-backed.
- Reranker: daytime-only reservation (2x H100) + autoscale to 0.5x using preemptible overnight is fine and we can implement cost-aware routing such that non-critical reranks use a cheaper model variant after hours.

Operational notes: we'll deliver an internal runbook for the canary (48–72h window) and pre-provision the capacity 7 days before cutover. I'll also flag the telemetry dashboards to track p95 and error budget.

If Rishi signs off I'll incorporate the 1x H100 buffer in the SOW as "optional resilience uplift" and price it as an add-on.

—Vivek

Katherine / BrightAtlas procurement —

Thanks for the quick responses. Attached are: (1) BrightAtlas_Dedicated_Expansion_Proposal_v3.pdf (breakout of reranker-hours and primary model costs) and (2) SOW_BrightAtlas_2028-08.pdf (includes migration plan, telemetry, and SLA appendix). Highlights:
- Base renewal (24 months): add 8x H100 (primary) + daytime-only 2x H100 reranker.
- Optional resilience uplift: +1x H100 (priced separately) to cover sustained peak headroom without touching preemptible pool.
- Throughput SLA: committed 600 tok/s aggregate; latency target p95 <350ms (SLA-penalty language included in appendix).
- Pricing: tiered discounting, quarterly invoicing preferred, Net30 billing terms.
- Onboarding: 4-week migration window with a one-month credit applied to first invoice for migration disruption.

DocuSign link to execute the SOW: https://www.docusign.com/sign?d=DA-7843-proposal
(also mirrored in HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/brightatlas/DA-7843)

Please let me know if procurement needs a formal quote PDF for PO submission or if this SOW + proposal is sufficient. If you want the optional +1x H100 included in the executed SOW, call that out and we'll update pricing.

Next steps: procurement confirms billing contact and preferred PO flow, Katherine confirms whether we should include the +1x buffer. Once we have PO or signature, we will schedule the pre-provisioning and canary window.

Thanks,
Rishi
